fullPassage: A simple truth that designers must embrace in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user. We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. The best user interfaces are those that have been shaped by observations of real users and their interactions with them. So how can designers shape their work to be more effective? An incredibly effective way is with usability testing. The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by asking participants to engage in realistic activities. This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users. Designers can use this method to improve their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from representative users.

questions.passage: A simple truth that designers must (A)[reject / embrace] in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user. We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. The best user interfaces are those that have been shaped by (B)[observations / assumptions] of real users and their interactions with them. So how can designers shape their work to be more effective? An incredibly effective way is with usability testing. The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by asking participants to engage in realistic activities. This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users. Designers can use this method to (C)[improve / worsen] their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from representative users.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 디자이너는 '우리는 사용자가 아니다'라는 진실을 받아들여야(embrace) 하고, 최고의 인터페이스는 실제 사용자에 대한 관찰(observations)로 만들어지며, 이 방법으로 작업을 개선할(improve) 수 있다는 내용이에요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① embrace — observations — improve: 본문과 정확히 일치해요 ←정답

❌ ② reject(거부하다): 디자이너가 진실을 '거부한다'가 아니라 '받아들여야(embrace)' 더 나은 제품을 만들 수 있어요

❌ ③ assumptions(추측): 최고의 인터페이스는 '추측'이 아니라 실제 사용자 '관찰(observations)'로 만들어져요

❌ ④ worsen(악화시키다): 디자이너는 작업을 '악화시키려고'가 아니라 '개선하려고(improve)' 이 방법을 써요
det.tip: embrace(받아들이다) ↔ reject(거부하다), observations(관찰) ↔ assumptions(추측), improve(개선하다) ↔ worsen(악화시키다)

questions.passage: A simple truth that designers must embrace in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user. We’re much too close to what we build to (A)[subjectively / objectively] see it and understand how users will interact with it. The best user interfaces are those that have been shaped by observations of real users and their interactions with them. So how can designers shape their work to be more effective? An incredibly effective way is with usability testing. The goal of this method is to (B)[uncover / hide] problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by asking participants to engage in realistic activities. This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users. Designers can use this method to improve their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from (C)[representative / random] users.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우리는 만든 것에 너무 가까워 객관적으로(objectively) 볼 수 없고, 사용성 테스트는 문제를 드러내며(uncover), 대표적인(representative) 사용자의 결과를 바탕으로 작업을 개선한다는 내용이에요.
det.analysis:
✅ ② objectively — uncover — representative: 본문과 정확히 일치 ←정답

❌ ① subjectively(주관적으로): 너무 가까워서 '객관적으로(objectively)' 못 본다는 게 핵심이라 반대예요

❌ ③ hide(숨기다): 이 방법의 목표는 문제를 '드러내는(uncover)' 것이지 '숨기는' 게 아니에요

❌ ④ random(무작위의): '무작위' 사용자가 아니라 '대표적인(representative)' 사용자의 결과를 바탕으로 해요
det.tip: objectively(객관적으로) ↔ subjectively(주관적으로), uncover(드러내다) ↔ hide(숨기다), representative(대표적인) ↔ random(무작위의)

We’re much too (A)[distant / close] to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 우리는 만든 것에 너무 가까워서(close) 객관적으로 못 보고, 사용성 테스트로 기회를 발견하며(discover), 그 다음의(subsequent) 수정을 통해 작업을 개선한다는 내용이에요.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ close — discover — subsequent: 본문과 정확히 일치 ←정답

❌ ① distant(멀리 떨어진): '너무 가까워서(close)' 객관적으로 못 본다는 맥락이라 반대예요

❌ ② overlook(간과하다): 기존 기회를 '간과한다'가 아니라 '발견한다(discover)'가 맞아요

❌ ④ previous(이전의): 테스트 결과를 바탕으로 한 건 '그 다음의(subsequent)' 수정이지 '이전의' 수정이 아니에요
det.tip: close(가까운) ↔ distant(먼), discover(발견하다) ↔ overlook(간과하다), subsequent(그 다음의) ↔ previous(이전의)

det.korean: ④ worsen(악화시키다) → improve(개선하다): 디자이너는 사용성 테스트 결과를 바탕으로 작업을 '개선하려고' 이 방법을 쓰는 것이므로, '악화시킨다'는 정반대예요.

det.tip: improve(개선하다) ↔ worsen(악화시키다). 수정(revisions)의 목적은 더 나아지게 하는 것이에요.

det.korean: ① reject(거부하다) → embrace(받아들이다): 더 효과적인 제품을 만들려면 '우리는 사용자가 아니다'라는 진실을 '받아들여야' 하므로, '거부한다'는 반대예요.

det.korean: ② hide(숨기다) → uncover(드러내다): 사용성 테스트의 목표는 디자인의 문제를 '드러내는' 것이므로, '숨긴다'는 정반대의 의미예요.

✅ ③ perform(작동하다): '디자인이 얼마나 잘 작동할지' — 본문과 일치

✅ ④ representative(대표적인): '대표적인 사용자의 결과' — 본문과 일치
det.tip: uncover(드러내다) ↔ hide(숨기다). 사용성 테스트는 숨은 문제를 찾아 드러내는 것이 목적이에요.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 improve와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: improve = 개선하다, 향상시키다. enhance = 향상시키다 → 동의어예요.
det.analysis:
❌ ① reduce(줄이다): 양을 줄이는 것으로 improve와 뜻이 달라요

❌ ② delay(미루다): 시간을 미루는 것으로 improve와 관련 없어요

❌ ③ repeat(반복하다): 다시 하는 것으로 '더 좋게 만드는' improve와 달라요

✅ ④ enhance(향상시키다): improve의 동의어, 둘 다 '질을 더 좋게 만들다'를 뜻해요 ←정답
det.tip: improve = enhance = refine(개선하다, 향상시키다). 수정(revisions)을 통해 작업을 더 좋게 만든다는 뜻이에요.

questions.passage: A simple truth that designers must embrace in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user. We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. The <u>best</u> user interfaces are those that have been shaped by observations of real users and their interactions with them. So how can designers shape their work to be more effective? An incredibly effective way is with usability testing. The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by asking participants to engage in realistic activities. This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users. Designers can use this method to improve their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from representative users.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 best와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: best = 최고의, 가장 좋은 ↔ worst = 최악의, 가장 나쁜
det.analysis:
✅ ① worst(최악의): best의 반의어예요. 가장 좋은 것의 정반대는 가장 나쁜 것이죠 ←정답

❌ ② similar(비슷한): 유사함을 뜻해서 best와 의미축이 달라요

❌ ③ frequent(빈번한): 빈도를 뜻해서 best와 의미축이 달라요

❌ ④ local(지역의): 장소를 뜻해서 best와 의미축이 달라요
det.tip: best(최고의) ↔ worst(최악의). the best user interfaces = 최고의 사용자 인터페이스

questions.passage: A simple truth that designers must embrace in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user. We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. The best user interfaces are those that have been shaped by observations of real users and their interactions with them. So how can designers shape their work to be more effective? An <u>incredibly</u> effective way is with usability testing. The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by asking participants to engage in realistic activities. This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users. Designers can use this method to improve their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from representative users.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 incredibly와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: incredibly = 엄청나게, 대단히 (정도가 큼) ↔ slightly = 약간, 조금 (정도가 작음)
det.analysis:
❌ ① extremely(극도로): '엄청나게'와 같은 방향(정도가 큼)이라 오히려 동의어예요 (함정!)

✅ ② slightly(약간): incredibly의 반의어예요. 정도가 '크다' ↔ '작다'로 대비돼요 ←정답

❌ ③ possibly(아마): 가능성을 뜻해서 '정도'를 나타내는 incredibly와 의미축이 달라요

❌ ④ clearly(분명히): 명확함을 뜻해서 incredibly와 의미축이 달라요
det.tip: incredibly(엄청나게) ↔ slightly(약간). extremely는 같은 '매우' 계열이라 반의어가 아닌 함정이에요.

questions.passage:
(A) Even under heavy traffic, a well-designed app can <u>perform</u> smoothly when thousands of real users log in at the same time.
(B) The young pianist was nervous but thrilled to <u>perform</u> on the big stage in front of a huge audience.
questions.stem: 다음 두 문장의 밑줄 친 perform의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) perform = (기계·시스템이) 작동하다, 기능하다. (B) perform = (무대에서) 공연하다, 연주하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 공연하다: (A)의 perform은 앱이 '작동한다'는 뜻이라 '공연하다'가 아니에요

❌ ② (A) 수술하다: (A)는 '작동하다'가 맞아 틀렸어요

✅ ③ (A): 작동하다 (B): 공연하다 — 두 문맥 모두 정확해요 ←정답

❌ ④ (B) 임무를 수행하다: (B)의 perform은 무대에서 '공연하다'라는 뜻이라 '임무를 수행하다'가 아니에요
det.tip: perform: (기계·시스템이) 작동하다(the app performs well), (무대에서) 공연하다(perform on stage), (수술을) 하다(perform surgery), (임무를) 수행하다(perform a task)

questions.stem:
다음 영영풀이에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은?
"a person who takes part in an activity, event, or study"

det.korean: 어떤 활동·행사·연구에 '참여하는 사람' = participant(참가자)
det.analysis:
❌ ① designer(디자이너): 무언가를 설계하는 사람으로, '참여하는 사람'이라는 정의와 달라요

❌ ② observer(관찰자): 지켜보는 사람으로, 활동에 '직접 참여하는' 사람은 아니에요

❌ ③ competitor(경쟁자): 경쟁하는 사람으로, 정의와 맞지 않아요

✅ ④ participant(참가자): 활동·연구에 참여하는 사람 — 정의와 정확히 일치 ←정답
det.tip: participant = 참가자. 본문의 asking participants to engage in realistic activities(참가자들에게 현실적인 활동을 하게 하다)에서 나온 단어예요.

questions.passage: The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by __________ (ask) participants to engage in realistic activities. This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰시오. (영어로)

The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by __________ (ask) participants to engage in realistic activities. This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users.

det.korean: 전치사 by 뒤에는 동사가 동명사(-ing) 형태로 와야 해요. ask → asking.
det.analysis: ✅ asking: 전치사 by 다음에는 명사나 동명사가 와야 하므로 ask를 동명사 asking으로 바꿔요. by asking participants = 참가자들에게 ~하게 함으로써.
det.tip: by + 동명사(-ing) = ~함으로써. ask → asking. 전치사 뒤 동사는 항상 -ing 형태예요.

questions.passage: We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. The best user interfaces are those that have been __________ (shape) by observations of real users and their interactions with them.
questions.stem:
다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꾸어 쓰시오. (영어로)

We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. The best user interfaces are those that have been __________ (shape) by observations of real users and their interactions with them.

det.korean: 현재완료 수동태 have been + 과거분사(p.p.) 구조예요. 인터페이스가 '만들어지는' 것이므로 shape → shaped.
det.analysis: ✅ shaped: have been __________ (shape) 구조에서 have been 뒤에는 과거분사가 와야 해요. 인터페이스가 스스로 만드는 게 아니라 관찰에 의해 '형성되는' 것이므로 수동태 have been shaped가 돼요.
det.tip: 현재완료 수동태 = have/has + been + 과거분사(p.p.). shape → shaped. have been shaped = 형성되어 왔다

questions.passage: A simple truth that designers must embrace in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user. We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. The best user interfaces are those that have been shaped by observations of real users and their interactions with them. So how can designers shape their work to be more effective? An incredibly effective way is with usability testing. The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by asking participants to engage in __________. This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users. Designers can use this method to improve their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from representative users.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 사용성 테스트는 참가자들에게 '__________에 참여하게' 해서 사용자의 행동과 선호를 알아내요. 실제 사용 상황을 알려면 현실적인 활동(realistic activities)을 하게 해야 해요.
det.analysis:
✅ ① realistic activities(현실적인 활동): engage in realistic activities(현실적인 활동에 참여하다) — 실제 사용 행동을 관찰하려는 목적과 일치 ←정답

❌ ② imaginary stories(상상의 이야기): 상상이 아니라 '현실적인' 활동이어야 실제 사용성을 알 수 있어요

❌ ③ written exams(필기 시험): 시험을 보게 하는 것은 사용성 테스트의 방식이 아니에요

❌ ④ silent breaks(조용한 휴식): 휴식을 취하게 하면 사용자의 행동을 관찰할 수 없어요
det.tip: engage in realistic activities = 현실적인 활동에 참여하다. 실제 사용 상황을 재현해야 사용자의 진짜 행동과 선호를 알 수 있어요.

questions.passage: A simple truth that designers must embrace in order to create more effective products and experiences is the fact that we are not the user. We’re much too close to what we build to objectively see it and understand how users will interact with it. The best user interfaces are those that have been shaped by observations of real users and their interactions with them. So how can designers shape their work to be more effective? An incredibly effective way is with __________. The goal of this method is to uncover problems in a design, discover existing opportunities, and learn more about the behaviors and preferences of users by asking participants to engage in realistic activities. This technique is effective for understanding how well a design will perform once it is in the hands of real users. Designers can use this method to improve their work through subsequent revisions based on the findings from representative users.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 디자이너가 작업을 더 효과적으로 다듬는 '엄청나게 효과적인 방법'은 __________이라고 했어요. 뒤에서 '참가자에게 현실적인 활동을 시켜 문제를 찾는' 방법이라고 설명하므로 사용성 테스트(usability testing)예요.
det.analysis:
❌ ① random guessing(무작위 추측): 뒤에 나오는 '참가자 관찰·문제 발견'이라는 체계적 방법과 맞지 않아요

✅ ② usability testing(사용성 테스트): 바로 뒤 '문제를 드러내고 기회를 발견하며 참가자의 행동을 관찰한다'는 설명이 이 방법을 정의해요 ←정답

❌ ③ personal opinion(개인적 의견): 실제 사용자를 관찰하는 방법이라 '개인 의견'과 반대예요

❌ ④ market advertising(시장 광고): 광고는 디자인을 테스트하는 방법이 아니에요
det.tip: usability testing = 사용성 테스트. 뒤 문장 전체(The goal of this method ...)가 이 방법이 무엇인지 풀어서 설명해 줘요.
